summary: Highly conductive SnO2 thin films were grown by atomic layer deposition (ALD) using tetrakis-dimethyl-amine tin (TDMASn) as a Sn precursor and ozone as an oxidizing reactant. The films showed excellent electrical properties (5.63 × 10−4 Ω cm) above 200 °C, with high carrier concentration and Hall mobility. The study focused on the effects of growth temperature on the properties of the films, including their crystallinity, surface morphology, and optical properties.
evidence: Highly conductive SnO2 thin ﬁlms were grown by atomic layer deposition (ALD) in a wide growth temperature range (50 °C –250 °C), using a tetrakis-dimethyl-amine tin (TDMASn) precursor and an ozone reactant. The ozone SnO2 ALD thin films showed excellent electrical properties (5.63 × 10−4 Ω cm) over 200 °C, but the electrical properties of the films were not measured at low growth temperature (under 125 °C).
